title: Silas and the Autopsy
premise: When a drowned man washes up at the Grand Meridian wearing clothes stolen from concierge Theo Sandoval's own closet, she becomes both suspect and the only witness who recognizes him — a guest who checked in three years ago and never left. Using her encyclopedic knowledge of the hotel's ledgers, keys, and staff secrets, Theo uncovers a cover-up reaching into the town's founding families, whose annual anniversary dinner will seal an inheritance built on the murder. As the police close in on her as their convenient culprit, Theo stages a trap at the dinner itself, forcing the killer — the hotel's beloved owner, who has been living under his dead brother's identity for years — to confess before the whole town. In the end, justice arrives outside any courtroom: the town chooses to remember, and Theo finds the family she never had among those willing to stand with her.
about_author: Theo Whitlock is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent a decade collecting the strange true stories of hotel lobbies. They write mysteries about ordinary people who see too much.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A body surfaces in the hotel fountain wearing Theo's own missing blazer, and she recognizes the face from a ledger entry three years old. The detective on scene treats her as a suspect; the staff treat her as family. Emotional beat: dread braided with fierce protectiveness of the hotel that raised her.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Interrogated by Detective Marsh, Theo realizes the victim was 'Mr. Ellery Voss,' a guest whose bill was quietly settled by the owner, Ambrose Hale. She begins cross-referencing ledgers at night. Emotional beat: the thrill of competence curdling as she finds pages razored out.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with housekeeper Marisol. The town prepares for the Hales' 50th-anniversary dinner while Theo learns the victim arrived the same week as the last one. Marisol reveals staff were paid to forget a fire in the east wing. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against fear.

chapters.title: A Room With No Key
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Room 412 has no key in existence, yet shows fresh use. Inside she finds photographs of herself, taken over months. Someone has been watching her since chapter one. Emotional beat: violation; the hotel stops feeling like home.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. The detective's private file suggests a drowning twelve years ago ruled accidental — a Hale brother. He suspects Theo knows more than she says and offers her a deal. Emotional beat: grudging mutual respect between two people who both notice everything.

chapters.title: The Second Blazer
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Another garment disappears from Theo's closet; the frame-up is accelerating. Marisol catches the night porter burning documents and is threatened. Emotional beat: terror, and the decision to stop being a bystander.

chapters.title: Brothers, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ledger forensics reveal 'Ambrose Hale' died a decade ago; the man running the hotel is his twin, Julian, who erased his brother and now erases anyone who remembers. Emotional beat: grief for the kind man she thought employed her, horror at what power did to him.

chapters.title: Cornered
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He offers Theo partnership — her discretion, his empire — and makes clear refusal means becoming the next body. She pretends to accept, buying time until the dinner. Emotional beat: cold clarity beneath performed compliance.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the anniversary dinner, Theo swaps the toast cards, plants the recovered ledger pages, and goads Julian into a public confession as Marsh and the town listen. Emotional beat: white-knuckle courage paying off in a single held breath.

chapters.title: New Keys
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Julian is arrested; the town reckons with its complicity. The staff, not investors, take over the Grand Meridian, and Theo cuts new keys — including one for room 412, reopened as a memorial. Emotional beat: found family solidified; justice outside the law honored inside it.
